Unfortunately, you really needed to specify that you meant JRPGs. You may be wondering why some of your comments are getting downvoted; that's because of your assertion that PS1 had the 'best RPGs' whereas, for many of us, the PC has and always will be the place to play WRPGs (Western RPGs).

Western CRPGs (Computer RPGs) predate all the consoles and inspired all the console classics like Dragon Warrior and Final Fantasy. WCRPGs and JRPGs evolved in parallel and were, despite sharing the same roots, extremely different. Whereas JRPGs almost all followed a very similar template, CRPGs were all over the place. When Final Fantasy 7 was 'revolutionalizing' the traditional JRPG format, Fallout 1 was coming out on PC, likewise changing the landscape. While JRPGs continued down a very traditional path, barely changing, CRPGs brought us The Elder Scrolls titles, the Infinity Engine games (Baldurs Gate, Icewind Dale, Planescape Torment), Divine Divinity, games that (because of the more versatile controls available on a PC, namely the mouse) had much more complicated interfaces, inventories, interactions, etc. Bioware, the makes of Mass Effect, started on PC, as did Bethesda (Elder Scrolls, Fallout 3).

I grew up with a PC, as did many other nerds on here I think, so we can't help but take a little offense at an entire rich history and evolution of gaming being discounted entirely. I am sure offense was not your intent, as the number of people involved in these games when they were new was relatively small. Personally I enjoy all the branches of RPG history, leaning towards consoles up till the late 90's when I got sick of the Squeenix model (or they just stopped making games I liked, except for FF9).
